experiment: Git-object bound evidence reuse across independent branches

scratch_branch_experiment.revision: actual two-parent merge combining reader and writer mutants

additional_tests: Changing a common source dependency invalidates both independent contract source closures and composition.
Deleting the reader module does not invalidate writer's isolated closure.
Explicit semantic claims propagate invalidation even if a contract's chosen source subset has no direct blob changes.
Changing reported oracle status to insufficient evidence cannot yield reuse eligibility.
Dynamic or unresolved imports block reusing static closure evidence.
Mismatched contract implementation blobs or unsupported prerequisites fail closed.
Duplicate revision selection and mismatched source evidence pins fail closed.
boundaries: Exact git blob identity and static source closure under a pinned basis, not a result of whole-program integration verification.
Previously published independent verification evidence is referenced from a summary and not rerun or externally authenticated in this experiment.
Source changes without behavioral effects can still require re-verification; this is a conservative false positive.
Unrelated added files, changed package initializers, environment differences, and dependency oracles can affect behavior outside the isolated-closure scope.
Scratch branch commits are disposable; existing upstream h11 master and contract-generated histories were never changed.
Git merge ancestry alone does not certify semantic composition.
interpretation: Evidence reuse is conditional on exact source-closure identity and explicit claim prerequisite eligibility, not whether two commits share ancestors or are topologically adjacent.
